title.en: Practice: Arrangements, blood relations, directions and coding
title.hi: अभ्यास: व्यवस्था, रक्त संबंध, दिशाएँ और कूट भाषा

section: Practice (written by us, not from a UPSC paper): Arrangements, blood relations, directions and coding

en.stem: Five friends A, B, C, D and E sit in a row facing north. A is at the left end. C is in the middle. B is to the immediate right of C. D is not at either end. Who sits at the right end?
en.why: Seats 1 to 5. A = 1, C = 3, B = 4. D is not at an end, so D = 2. E takes seat 5, the right end.

en.stem: Six people P, Q, R, S, T and U sit round a table facing the centre. P is opposite S. Q is to the immediate right of P. T is opposite Q. R is to the immediate left of P. Who is opposite R?
en.why: Number the seats 0 to 5 clockwise. P = 0, S = 3. Right is anticlockwise, so Q = 5 and T, opposite Q, = 2. Left is clockwise, so R = 1. U takes seat 4, which is opposite seat 1.

en.stem: In a row of 40 students, Ravi is 12th from the left end. What is his position from the right end?
en.why: Position from the right = 40 - 12 + 1 = 29. Check: 11 students to his left and 28 to his right, plus Ravi, make 40.

en.stem: A is taller than B. C is shorter than B. D is taller than A. Who is the shortest?
en.why: Order from tallest: D, A, B, C. The shortest is C.

en.stem: Pointing to a woman, Arun says, "Her mother is the only daughter of my mother." How is the woman related to Arun?
en.why: The only daughter of Arun's mother is Arun's sister. The woman is his sister's daughter, that is, his niece.

en.stem: A is B's brother. C is A's mother. D is C's father. How is B related to D?
options: Grandchild; the gender is not known
en.why: A and B are children of C, and D is C's father, so B is D's grandchild. A is B's brother fixes A's gender only, so B may be a grandson or a granddaughter.

en.stem: P is the father of Q. Q is the sister of R. R is the husband of S. How is S related to P?
en.why: Q and R are brother and sister, so P is also R's father. S is the wife of P's son R, so S is P's daughter-in-law.

en.stem: A man walks 3 km north, turns right and walks 4 km. How far is he from his starting point?
en.why: He is 3 km north and 4 km east of the start. The straight distance is the hypotenuse of a 3, 4, 5 triangle: 5 km. Seven is the distance walked, not the distance from the start.

en.stem: A woman is facing east. She turns left, then turns right, and then turns about. Which direction is she facing now?
en.why: East, left turn: north. Right turn: east. About turn: west.

en.stem: A boy walks 10 m south, turns left and walks 6 m, then turns left again and walks 10 m. Where is he now with respect to his starting point?
en.why: Facing south, a left turn points east: 6 m east. Another left turn points north: 10 m north, which cancels the 10 m south. He is 6 m east of the start.

en.stem: Soon after sunrise, Rita stands in an open field and sees her shadow falling to her right. Which direction is she facing?
en.why: In the morning the sun is in the east and shadows fall west. West is to her right, so she is facing south.

en.stem: In a certain code, CAT is written as DBU. How is DOG written in that code?
en.why: Each letter moves one place forward: C to D, A to B, T to U. So D to E, O to P, G to H: EPH.

en.stem: If A = 1, B = 2 and so on, and the code for a word is the sum of its letters, the code for BAD is 7. What is the code for CAB?
en.why: Check the rule: B + A + D = 2 + 1 + 4 = 7. Then C + A + B = 3 + 1 + 2 = 6.

en.stem: In a code, each letter is replaced by its opposite letter in the alphabet, so that A becomes Z and B becomes Y. How is GO written?
en.why: Opposite letters add up to 27. G is 7, so its opposite is 20, T. O is 15, so its opposite is 12, L. The code is TL.

en.stem: If red is called blue, blue is called green, and green is called white, what is the colour of grass called?
en.why: Grass is green. In this code green is called white. Stop there; do not ask what white is called.
